subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 60-year-old man is studied after a protein-rich meal. Hepatic N-acetylglutamate, synthesized from glutamate and acetyl-CoA by N-acetylglutamate synthase, increases and stimulates carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I, accelerating ureagenesis.
question: Activity of N-acetylglutamate synthase is most directly increased by which of the following?
explanation_correct: Arginine allosterically activates N-acetylglutamate synthase, which raises N-acetylglutamate and stimulates carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I; this signals an abundant supply of amino acid nitrogen. Arginine is therefore also used therapeutically in several urea cycle disorders to enhance residual cycle activity.

explanation_incorrect.A: Citrulline is a downstream urea cycle intermediate and does not activate N-acetylglutamate synthase.
explanation_incorrect.B: Urea is the excreted end product and has no stimulatory effect on this enzyme.
explanation_incorrect.D: Ammonia is the substrate of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I, not an activator of N-acetylglutamate synthase.
explanation_incorrect.E: Aspartate donates the second urea nitrogen at a later step and does not activate this enzyme.

educationalObjective: Arginine activates N-acetylglutamate synthase, increasing N-acetylglutamate and stimulating carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I.
